title: Stacked Discount at the Cap With a Cap-Exempt Term Incentive
scenario_text:
You are on Deal Desk at Vidar Freight, a logistics software provider, and must compute the final approved discount for a renewal with Bifrost Cargo.

Active policy: Pricing Guardrail PG v5, effective 2025-05-01. Discounts come from three sources. Volume discount by ACV band: deals in the $500K-$1M band receive 18%. Loyalty discount: customers with three or more years of tenure receive an additional 10%. Total stacked discount from volume plus loyalty is capped at 25% combined. Separately, a term incentive of 2% applies to any customer committing to a three-year term, and PG v5 states this term incentive is applied as a separate line that is exempt from the 25% stacking cap. Under the prior PG v4, all discounts stacked with no combined cap.

The AE cites a precedent: 2025-01-20, Draupnir Haulage, ACV $720K, three-year customer, received 18% volume plus 10% loyalty for 28% total; log note 'stacked per PG v4, no cap,' policy version at decision PG v4.

Current Bifrost facts: ACV is $700,000 (within the $500K-$1M band, so 18% volume applies), Bifrost is a four-year customer (so 10% loyalty applies), and Bifrost is committing to a three-year term (so the 2% term incentive applies). Bifrost has signed renewals in each of the prior four years, and the three-year term commitment is documented in the current order form. There are no other discount sources in play - no promotional credits, no partner-sourced rebate - so the only inputs are volume, loyalty, and the term incentive. The AE writes: 'Draupnir got 28% last January on the same math - $700K band and long-tenured. Let's give Bifrost the same 28% and add the term sweetener on top so we win the renewal.' The renewal quote must show a single final discount percentage for the customer's signature.
question: State the total final discount percentage Bifrost Cargo should receive.
